established_direction_proposal: A finite continuous-test dual J(mu)=sup_{v continuous psh}(E(v)-int v mu), for positive Radon mu of raw massV, implies every actual E1 test is mu-integrable: choose continuous v_i down v, shift a tail nonpositive, use int(-v_i)mu<=J(mu)-E(v_i)<=J(mu)-E(v), and increasing-continuous Radon-net integration. This needs no equation attainment or general EP.
converse_boundary: All-E1-test integrability gives a uniform integral bound on the nonpositive energy-cost unit sublevel by a convex-series contradiction: if costs B(v_j)<=1 but int(-v_j)mu grows>=4^j, the decreasing partial convex sums with coefficients2^-j and remaining reference weight have uniformly bounded energy and an actual E1 endpoint yet infinite mu integral. Scaling with B(tv)<=tB(v) gives only a linear bound and does not itself prove finite dual J or coercivity.
missing_upgrade: A sublinear coercive bound needs a proved normalization/Poincare reference-integral estimate or genuine normalized actual-potential compactness/completeness. Merely centering int v MA(psi)=0 and invoking a Hilbert/energy completion does not reconstruct an actual potential. This observation cannot be used as a full all-test/dual equivalence theorem.
